title: Make it your lake
intro: Keep the activities. Change the evidence and the local story.

sections.title: Start with the lake configuration
paragraphs: Copy config/lady-bird-lake.json. Give your lake a new ID, name, coordinates, monitoring sites, agency links and outline. Point app.js at your new file.

The dataPaths mapping replaces station data files. Use the same documented columns or adapt the station module. Map geometry must be projected to metres; imagery and geometry must share a coordinate reference system.

sections.title: Freeze evidence you may reuse
paragraphs: Use a script in scripts/ to fetch openly licensed records once. Preserve dates, units, sample types, qualifiers and source identifiers. Add a README and metadata with retrieval date, author, licence, cleaning and gaps.
Update data/manifest.json and run scripts/validate.py. Never relabel a simulation as a local measurement. Review the source terms again when refreshing.

sections.title: Adapt the lessons
paragraphs: Edit challenges, hints, explanations and project questions in content/en/. Disable unsupported stations in config. Review teaching assumptions and local bloom types with an expert.
The current satellite panel, selected units and source-specific cleaning rules need adaptation for another lake. See README and docs/methods.md; changing the lake name alone is not enough.

sections.title: Publish and test
paragraphs: Keep MIT code and content attribution, and preserve each external asset’s licence. Test phones, keyboard controls, missing data and unavailable browser storage.
Publish the folder root on GitHub Pages. All data and assets must stay on the same site; do not add live API calls or tracking.
